name: aws_eks_cluster
description: Manages an EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) cluster. EKS is a managed Kubernetes service that runs the Kubernetes control plane across multiple AWS Availability Zones. It handles control plane node management, patching, and availability automatically.
use_cases: Run stateful applications with persistent storage
Multi-team Kubernetes cluster with RBAC isolation

required.name: name
required.description: Name of the EKS cluster. Must be unique within an AWS region.

required.name: role_arn
required.description: ARN of the IAM role that provides permissions for EKS to manage AWS resources. Must include AmazonEKSClusterPolicy.

required.name: vpc_config
required.description: Network configuration for the cluster. Requires subnet_ids (at least 2 in different AZs).

optional.name: version
optional.description: Kubernetes version. Recommended: always specify explicitly. Example: '1.29'

optional.name: enabled_cluster_log_types
optional.description: List of control plane logging types: api, audit, authenticator, controllerManager, scheduler.

optional.name: encryption_config
optional.description: KMS encryption configuration for Kubernetes secrets.

optional.name: tags
optional.description: Map of tags to assign to the cluster.

best_practices: Always specify the Kubernetes version explicitly — avoid automatic upgrades
Place nodes in private subnets only — ALB handles public traffic
Enable control plane logging (at minimum api, audit, authenticator)
Use managed node groups (aws_eks_node_group) instead of self-managed EC2
Enable secrets encryption with KMS for compliance
Use Cluster Autoscaler or Karpenter for dynamic node scaling
Set up IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) for pod-level permissions
Use private endpoint access with restricted public access CIDRs in production
Keep cluster and node group versions in sync (max 1 minor version skew)
security_notes: Restrict endpoint_public_access_cidrs to known IP ranges in production
Enable envelope encryption for Kubernetes secrets using KMS
Use IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) instead of node-level IAM roles
Implement Kubernetes RBAC policies from day one
Use Amazon VPC CNI with security groups for pods for network-level isolation
Enable EKS audit logging and ship to CloudWatch or S3 for compliance

common_errors.fix: Provide subnets in at least 2 different Availability Zones for the EKS control plane
EKS cluster creation can take 10-15 minutes. Set a longer timeout or increase Terraform timeout
Check node IAM role policies (AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy, AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy) and security group rules
